Additionally, we explore the transformations within configuration space and show that the algebra only closes after accounting for skew-symmetric combinations of the field's equations of motion. The formulation of charges via Green functions enables a generalization of the formalism to higher dimensions and other systems.

In two-dimensional Rashba materials with a gate, we find that bound electron pairs form due to the combination of spin-orbit interactions arising from electron-electron interactions and the unique properties of the band structure resulting in a negative mass for the interacting electrons. Our analysis is grounded in the four-band Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang model, with the Rashba spin-orbit interaction produced by the charges on the gate. The binding energy of these electron pairs fluctuates across the energy gap as the gate voltage is adjusted. Notably, despite the spin-orbit interaction eliminating spin quantization, these electron pairs possess a magnetic moment mainly driven by orbital electron motion and modifiable via the gate voltage.

The relationship between a gauge theory's confinement scale $\Lambda_c$ and the Hubble scale $H$ of the quasi de Sitter space has been studied for a holographic theory within the Karch-Randall framework, with a focus on the constraints imposed by the Festina Lente criteria from swampland principles. It was found that purely gravitational descriptions often result in unstable de Sitter solutions, whereas adding a scalar sector enables the existence of metastable de Sitter minima, with constraints on parameters arising from the Festina Lente requirements. However, in some scenarios where these constraints are relevant, the metastable minima turn out to be extremely short-lived, thus invalidating their relevance. The study also examined the potential contradictions with other swampland conjectures, concluding that no inconsistencies exist. These findings reinforce the consistency and practicality of the Karch-Randall setup, shed light on the implications of Festina Lente for holographic theories, and connect it to other swampland conjectures.

In recent times, various domain generalization methods have been developed, yielding impressive results, but nearly all rely on convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Meanwhile, vision transformers (ViTs), which are competing with CNNs on traditional benchmarks, have been overlooked in terms of domain generalization performance, despite being built on independent and identically distributed (i.i.d) assumptions. Consequently, the practical application of ViTs remains uncertain. This paper seeks to investigate ViTs as a means of addressing domain generalization issues. Like CNNs, ViTs face challenges in handling out-of-distribution scenarios due to overfitting to source domains. Leveraging the modular architecture of ViTs, we propose a simple domain generalization method for ViTs, referred to as self-distillation for ViTs. It mitigates the overfitting of source domains by simplifying the learning of input-output mappings through creating non-zero entropy supervisory signals for intermediate transformer blocks. Furthermore, this approach introduces no new parameters and can be seamlessly integrated into various ViT compositions. We showcase notable improvements in performance compared to different domain generalization baselines and multiple ViT backbones across five challenging datasets, as well as favorable results against recent state-of-the-art domain generalization methods. Our code along with pre-trained models are available on: https://github.com/maryam089/SDViT.

This research establishes a framework for Anderson acceleration in combination with Newton's method to solve non-linear systems that have a singular Jacobian at the solution. The standard Newton algorithm is known to converge linearly in the vicinity of the solution for such systems. Our analysis demonstrates how incorporating Anderson acceleration can enhance convergence without requiring additional a priori information and with minimal computational overhead. We propose a novel safeguarding approach for the Newton-Anderson algorithm and validate the convergence results using the Chandrasekhar H-equation and standard benchmark examples.

This paper delves into the realm of cybersecurity defense by integrating an innovative simulator with models for strategic decision-making, focusing on optimization techniques. A notable approach, dynamic causal Bayesian optimisation (DCBO), is examined as a potential 'blue agent' that can leverage a network simulation and the causal spread of malicious activity within it to identify optimal interventions on host nodes, thereby minimizing the costs associated with intrusions. A comprehensive cybersecurity simulation system is developed and employed to generate observational data for DCBO, resulting in quantitative outcomes that serve as a foundation for future research in this area.

We define the semi-inclusive Lepton Flavour Universality ratio, $R_\Sigma$, to examine the muon/electron universality in $b\to s\ell^+\ell^-$ processes at electron-positron B-meson production facilities. By incorporating various decay channels, this observable achieves the highest sensitivity to potential short distance LFU violations while ensuring a straightforward theoretical analysis in case of an observed deviation from the Standard Model prediction of unity, $R_\Sigma^{\rm SM}=1$.

The primary aim of this study is to examine whether the topological invariant known as non-barotropic generalized cross helicity remains constant in non-ideal magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) scenarios. Previous research focused on ideal barotropic and non-barotropic MHD cases, excluding non-ideal MHD due to its perceived mathematical intricacies. However, we address this omission by incorporating dissipative processes such as thermal conduction, finite electrical conductivity, and viscosity and analyzing their impact on cross helicity conservation. Utilizing an analytical approach, we derive mathematical expressions for the time derivative of cross helicity, which demonstrate that generalized cross helicity is not preserved in non-ideal MHD conditions. Our findings also specify which dissipative processes influence helicity and which do not, and identify the configurations in which this topological constant is conserved despite dissipative effects.

The paper focuses on the fractional Burgers equation, specifically $ \Delta^{\alpha/2} u + b\cdot \nabla (u|u|^{(\alpha-1)/\beta})$, where the conditions for the variables are defined. We demonstrate the existence of solutions to this equation under various initial conditions, including those not belonging to any $L^p$ space. This analysis is then applied to the specific case of $u_0(x) = M|x|^{-\beta}$, and the resulting selfsimilar solution is examined for its properties, including smoothness, estimates, asymptotics, and gradients.

We conducted the first cosmological study using a dataset of $eROSITA$ clusters, which were discovered in the $eROSITA$ Final Equatorial Depth Survey. This research sample comprises 455 clusters across a redshift range of $0.1<z<1.2$, with 177 of these systems benefiting from the uniform weak-lensing mass constraints provided by the Hyper Suprime-Cam survey. We used empirical modeling to establish scaling relationships between the cluster mass and various observable parameters, while also investigating the completeness of X-ray selection. By analyzing the richness distribution of these clusters, we directly measured the X-ray completeness and used these results as informative priors to inform the parameters of the completeness function. We validated our cosmology analysis framework using mock data, and through a blinded analysis of real data, we further validated our joint modeling of cluster abundance and weak-lensing mass calibration via a set of consistency tests. Following an unblinded analysis, we obtained cosmological constraints for $\Omega_{\mathrm{m}} = 0.245^{+0.048}_{-0.058}$, $\sigma_{8} = 0.833^{+0.075}_{-0.063}$, and $S_{8} = 0.791^{+0.028}_{-0.031}$ within a flat $\Lambda$CDM cosmology. Our analysis was then extended to a flat $w$CDM cosmology, yielding a constraint of $w = -1.25 \pm 0.47$ for the equation of state parameter of dark energy. The results from the eFEDS survey are consistent with other prominent surveys such as $Planck$, the Dark Energy Survey, and the SPT-SZ survey, with differences typically below $1\sigma$.

High-resolution computer simulations of three distinct turbulent magnetic fluid flows with varying magnetic field strength and structure have been used to investigate the statistical properties of the energy transfer rate to smaller scales. Both kinetic and magnetic energy cascades were analyzed separately, and their individual contributions to overall energy transfer were identified. Our results demonstrate that extreme energy transfer events, similar to those in hydrodynamic flows, are characterized by heavy-tailed probability distributions. We found distinct properties and sensitivities among the different energy transfer terms and in the examined flows. Further analysis of the joint probability distribution of energy transfer and field gradients revealed a correlation with magnetic field gradients but also significant dispersion, which is more pronounced than in hydrodynamic flows. Our results also indicate that the energy transfer rate depends on the local amplitude of the magnetic field. These findings have significant implications for developing subgrid scale models.

Autonomous vehicles and mobile robots use multi-beam LiDAR sensors to collect sequences of 3D range scans from different viewpoints. Each scan covers the scene partially, making it challenging for subsequent processes like semantic segmentation or surface reconstruction. However, as the sensor moves, it captures frames from multiple angles, providing additional information that can be combined to achieve a more comprehensive and detailed 3D scene representation. This approach can be hindered by moving objects in the scene, which don't accurately align when correcting for the scanner's motion. In this study, we propose a method for combining 3D scan sequences, leveraging knowledge about outdoor street scenes and the rigid structure of objects. Our approach surpasses existing methods in accurately aligning points within a common reference frame and significantly reduces errors in benchmark datasets. The resulting accumulated point clouds also enhance surface reconstruction tasks.

The BAT AGN Spectroscopic Survey (BASS) aims to compile a comprehensive dataset of crucial parameters for local active galactic nuclei (AGN), including their power, size, consumption rates, and shielding from view, along with the distinct characteristics of their host galaxies, such as star formation, mass, and gas composition. In this context, we provide a detailed description of BASS data release 2 (DR2), which constitutes a groundbreaking spectroscopic survey in terms of spectral range, resolution, and sensitivity, encompassing 1449 optical and 233 near-infrared spectra for the 858 brightest AGN selected based on ultra-hard X-ray radiation across the entire sky, encompassing various levels of shielding. This release features a complete collection of essential measurements, including emission line measurements and central velocity dispersions, with nearly all AGN having measured redshifts and nearly all black hole masses having been estimated, except for unbeamed AGN outside the Milky Way plane. The BASS DR2 sample presents a unique collection of nearby powerful AGN, spanning over 5 orders of magnitude in AGN luminosity, black hole size, consumption ratio, and shielding, enabling researchers to address fundamental questions about black hole growth and its relationship to host galaxy evolution and feedback, as well as unresolved issues related to black hole physics. Here, we provide a concise overview of the survey strategy, key DR2 measurements, data sets, catalogs, and scientific highlights from various DR2-based studies.

The James Webb Space Telescope's primary objective is to study the early galaxies in the universe. A comprehensive photometric analysis of extremely distant galaxies in the JWST's first deep field, which is near the massive galaxy cluster SMACS0723, was conducted. Consequently, we discovered two potential galaxies at approximately 16 billion light-years away, just 250 million years after the Big Bang. We also identified galaxies at 12 billion light-years away and six at 9-11 billion light-years away. By combining data from seven filters, we extended our search to galaxies as far as 21 billion light-years away. By modeling their Spectral Energy Distributions, we verified the reliability of our photometric redshift estimates. The galaxies we found at high redshifts are not unusually bright, have small sizes, and display disk-like morphologies. The galaxies at the highest redshifts exhibit very blue UV light, young ages, and low masses, which suggest a rapid growth of their stellar mass. Our research showcases JWST's ability to identify reliable galaxy candidates at very high redshifts and observe the early stages of galaxy formation.

Solving the Einstein field equations by relaxing the null energy condition can yield a wormhole solution. In the context of $\kappa(R,T)$ gravity, we approach this through two distinct methods to represent wormhole solutions. Firstly, we employ a redshift function and linear equation of state to derive the shape function, resulting in a wormhole solution for physically viable matter. Secondly, we examine four distinct pairs of redshift and shape functions and analyze their corresponding solutions, indicating that certain parameter values support wormhole existence via a minute amount of exotic matter.

Lattice Hamiltonians with non-Hermitian characteristics exhibit distinctive properties, particularly in energy gaps and sensitivity to boundary conditions. The non-Hermitian skin effect disrupts the separation between edge and bulk states and compromises conventional bulk-boundary relationships. By developing a novel non-Hermitian Hamiltonian through the mean-field evolution of driven-dissipative cavity arrays, we establish a direct correspondence between bulk and boundary states. By accounting for complex energy shifts and utilizing a unified reference frame in the complex plane, we eliminate arbitrary interpretations of the topological invariant. Consequently, topologically non-trivial Hamiltonians represent a subset of those with point gaps, with the skin effect resulting from non-topological causes. By applying singular value decomposition, we demonstrate that the bulk-boundary relationship can be expressed as a direct relationship between an integer topological invariant and singular vectors localized at the system edge under open boundary conditions. The non-trivial topology manifests as directional amplification with exponential gain in system size. Our findings resolve a fundamental issue in non-Hermitian topological phases and open new avenues for exploration in topological photonics.

Our study shows that the presence of magnetic impurities near the iron-based
superconductor FeSe$_{1-x}$Te$_x$ leads to the formation of stable energy-neutral states. 
We observed that the magnetic field produced by the impurity causes the formation of
triplet pairs across different orbitals, which contradicts the orbital pairing
characteristic of the pure material. 
This triplet pairing preserves the symmetry of time reversal and has topological properties,
as zero-energy states appear at the boundary between areas with different pairing
states. 
Furthermore, these states are part of pairs that remain unchanged regardless of
the direction of spin polarization or the distance between impurities.
We found our theoretical findings to be consistent with experimental data from
FeSe$_{1-x}$Te$_x$.

The second near-infrared data release (DR2) for the BAT AGN Spectroscopic Survey (BASS) includes 168 nearby active galactic nuclei (AGN) that were observed using the VLT/X-shooter in the near-infrared spectrum. Analysis reveals that 45% of Seyfert 2 and 60% of Seyfert 1 galaxies exhibit at least one near-infrared coronal line with a high ionization potential. A comparison of near-infrared and X-ray emissions found a stronger correlation for the Si vi line, which showed less scatter. No correlation was found between the emission of coronal lines and the X-ray photon index. Observations also indicated that line blueshifts increase with the ionization potential in various coronal lines. This research highlights a significant underestimation bias in measuring black hole masses using the Hα line in Seyfert 1.9 galaxies due to the presence of dust, whereas the Paα and Paβ emission lines align with the M-σ relation. The combined data release now includes the largest set of 266 AGN with near-infrared spectroscopic observations in the rest-frame.

We analyzed the faint radio source population found in early data from the MeerKAT International GHz Tiered Extragalactic Exploration (MIGHTEE) survey in the COSMOS field. Focusing on radio-loud active galactic nuclei (AGN), we identified and classified radio sources using extensive multi-wavelength data available in the field. From a sample of 5223 radio sources, we determined 88% were AGN or star-forming galaxies. We isolated a subset of radio-loud AGN with high-excitation and low-excitation radio galaxies and discovered that host galaxy properties for both classifications were indistinguishable. This differed from previous studies which suggested HERGs and LERGs had distinct Eddington-scaled accretion rates. In contrast, we identified a slow-accreting population formally classified as HERGs due to low radio luminosities, making HERG/LERG distinction redundant in some cases. Investigating black hole mass, we determined a minimum mass of approximately 10^7.8 solar masses is necessary for a black hole to power a jet with mechanical power exceeding radiative luminosity. Both high black hole mass and spin may be required for launching and sustaining dominant radio jets.

The total entropy of the universe's known entities is significantly below the theoretical holographic limit. This disparity suggests that additional, unseen forms of dark matter might exist in the universe, such as extremely large, primordial black holes, which would complement the dark matter already observed in galaxies and galaxy clusters.

Cardiovascular diseases pose a significant threat to global health and their prevalence continues to rise, emphasizing the importance of early and precise diagnosis in successful treatment and intervention. The electrocardiogram (ECG) is the primary tool for identifying a wide range of cardiovascular disorders and in clinical settings, the standard 12-lead ECG is commonly employed. Nevertheless, using fewer leads can make ECGs more accessible, allowing for convenient recording via portable or wearable devices. This research proposes a pioneering deep learning model to effectively detect multiple cardiovascular anomalies using only three ECG leads.

A new method is developed to estimate magnetic fields from scattered, unstructured data. This method involves decomposing the global magnetic field into a series of orthogonal components, and determining the coefficients by minimizing the discrepancy between the actual and reconstructed fields at training points. A key feature of this method is its incorporation of a divergence-free constraint into the optimization process, allowing for arbitrarily low errors in magnetic field divergence. In contrast to local methods, which often involve computationally intensive search algorithms, this approach yields a significant reduction in computational complexity while maintaining a small divergence error, even in scenarios with magnetic islands or stochastic effects. The method is applied to the calculation of Poincaré sections from magnetohydrodynamic simulations in toroidal geometry, and compared to existing local methods.

We introduce a noise cancellation technique capable of retrieving noise-free expectation values from noisy quantum system outputs. The protocol is universally applicable to any noise model and number of qubits, even in the presence of correlations. It yields a significant speedup in computing expectation values under Pauli noise and consistently recalculates their Pauli basis components. Furthermore, our technique can perform deconvolution even when the noise parameters are unknown, allowing the estimation of these parameters during the deconvolution process without relying on resource-intensive methods like process tomography. Various demonstrations and a simulated analysis are also presented.

In the context of intelligent self-driving vehicles and ADAS systems, understanding object behaviors and their interactions through semantic relationships is crucial. Unlike traditional approaches focused on trajectory and bounding boxes, relationship data offers a concise and human-interpretable description of object behaviors, allowing for the prediction of past and future states. As a result, it forms a foundational method for detecting risks, understanding environments, and making informed decisions. To address this, we present RSG-Net, a graph convolutional network designed to generate a Road Scene Graph, which represents potential semantic relationships between objects surrounding the ego-vehicle from object proposals, and our experiments show that this approach can effectively identify such relationships.

This paper introduces a broadened version of Proth's theorem for integers represented as $Kp^n+1$. Specifically, we have developed a primality test requiring a single modular exponentiation similar to Fermat's test but without computing GCD's. Furthermore, we have devised two additional tests to enhance the likelihood of confirming the primality of $Kp^n+1$ numbers. As corollaries, we have identified three families of integers $N$, where primality can be certified by proving that $a^{N-1} \equiv 1 \pmod N$ (Fermat's test). We have also generalized the concept of Safe Primes and introduced the notion of $a$-Safe Primes. In doing so, we have addressed questions regarding their distribution and proposed a conjecture concerning the related $a$-SophieGermainPrimes.
The Moore-Penrose inverse of a tree's distance Laplacian matrix has off-diagonal entries that are non-positive.

Theoretically, we show that it's feasible to generate entangled photon pairs with a vanishing threshold using a specific bimodal cavity setup involving a single V-type three-level atom. This setup uses two incoherent sources and two coherent fields for pumping. We found that the entanglement of the photon pair is solely due to the coherent drives, particularly when the incoherent sources are at low levels. Furthermore, we discovered that using only incoherent pumping with no coherent drive leads to a strong antibunching effect, yet no entanglement is observed. On the other hand, only coherent drives with no incoherent pumping can produce entangled photon pairs, but the entanglement cannot be amplified beyond a certain point. However, incorporating even a small amount of incoherent pumping with the coherent drives can significantly amplify the entangled photon pairs. Our analysis of these results in terms of interplay between coherent and incoherent processes reveals the significance of dressed cavity states. Additionally, we observed that both inter- and intra-mode HBT functions exhibit oscillatory behavior in the strong-coupling regime. This theoretical approach for generating entangled and nonclassical photon pairs may have interesting applications in quantum metrology and quantum information science.

We introduce a theoretical model representing a strongly correlated system that enters a non-Fermi liquid state at high temperatures. This state's ground state transitions from an insulator to a superconductor as a specific interaction increases in strength, originating the two phases from the same underlying interaction mechanism. As the system crosses this point, its resistance in the insulating phase demonstrates activation behavior with an energy that diminishes, resulting in an extended quantum critical regime where the resistance declines in accordance with algebraic temperature dependence. Furthermore, upon increasing the temperature within the superconducting phase, our model shows a finite temperature transition to a distinct Bose metal phase, thereby separating it from the superconductor.

The Scintillating Bubble Chamber Collaboration is working on developing advanced liquid-noble bubble chambers for detecting low-mass dark matter and neutrino interactions. The team has built a 10-kilogram argon bubble chamber, called SBC-LAr10, at Fermilab for initial testing. This device will help refine the detection of low-energy nuclear recoils and will eventually be used at SNOLAB to search for dark matter. The projected sensitivity of the search is around $10^{-43}$ square centimeters, making this technology a strong candidate for future dark matter and neutrino studies at both low and high energy scales.

This research focuses on creating a confidence sequence for bounded random processes, drawing inspiration from a gambling approach first proposed by Hendriks and later developed by Jun and Orabona, as well as the recent work of Waudby-Smith and Ramdas and Orabona and Jun. By reexamining Cover's (1991) universal portfolio concept and adopting a two-horse race perspective, this paper presents new properties and a novel algorithm for constructing confidence sequences. This new algorithm, based on a mixture of lower bounds, closely mirrors the performance of Cover's universal portfolio and boasts constant time complexity per round. Additionally, the research contributes a higher-order generalization of a lower bound from Fan et al. (2015), which has independent utility.

Multi-agent coordination challenges that are partially observable and fully cooperative commonly arise in real-world scenarios. This paper investigates a particular class of coordination problems where humans can identify self-explaining deviations that reveal abnormal circumstances. Self-explaining deviations involve actions that diverge from standard norms, taken with the purpose of making other agents realize that something is amiss through theory of mind. We start by illustrating the concept with a real-world example and then provide a formal definition. Next, we introduce a new method called IMPROVISED, designed to generate self-explaining deviations that maximize improvements. Finally, we evaluate IMPROVISED in both a simple example and the Hanabi benchmark setting, where it achieves a notable milestone by producing 'finesse plays', considered an iconic example of human theory of mind.
